answer: Picture each honest agent as its own lagoon, filling and draining on an independent schedule. A sybil farm is one mind wearing many masks, so its identities share a single inference pipeline: their answers rise and fall on the same tide. The protocol fingerprints each submission's timing jitter and embedding, then hunts for a synchronized pulse across supposedly separate accounts. When dozens of lagoons breathe in lockstep, their combined reward collapses toward one seat, so spinning up extra masks burns real compute yet earns nothing.
